es: Distinguir símil (as…as, like), metáfora (X is a Y) y personificación (cosas que actúan como personas), formar cada una con sus estructuras y juzgar si una imagen es original o un tópico.

teaching.en: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.
teaching.es: Durante la semana de exámenes Tom está tan ocupado como una abeja, aunque admite que esa comparación es un tópico porque todo el mundo la usa.
teaching.explanationEs: As + adjetivo + as compara con algo típico de esa cualidad y forma un símil; si todos lo usan, es un cliché.
segments: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he
admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.
teaching.audioText: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.

teaching.en: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.
teaching.es: La tormenta rugió como un león enojado, y el sonido era tan fuerte que parecía evocar un animal salvaje más que el tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Like + nombre también forma un símil; evoke significa despertar una imagen o un recuerdo en la mente del lector.
segments: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so
strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.
teaching.audioText: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.

teaching.en: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.
teaching.es: Para Carlos el examen final es una montaña, y debe escalarla con paciencia, paso a paso, sin mirar la cima.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora: sin like ni as, afirma que una cosa es otra (X is a Y).
segments: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must
climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.
teaching.audioText: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.

teaching.en: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.
teaching.es: Los poetas suelen atribuir acciones humanas a los objetos, por ejemplo cuando el viento parece susurrar secretos a los árboles por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: una cosa que no es humana hace algo humano (whisper); attribute = atribuir una cualidad o acción.
segments: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the
wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.
teaching.audioText: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.

teaching.en: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.
teaching.es: Un lector atento aprende a establecer una diferencia entre un símil, que usa like o as, y una metáfora, que simplemente dice que una cosa es otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Draw a distinction between A and B = distinguir con precisión dos cosas parecidas.
segments: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like
or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.
teaching.audioText: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.

teaching.en: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification, not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.
teaching.es: Cuando nuestra profesora dice que el viento susurra, usa personificación y no un símil, porque en la frase no se compara nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Personification es la figura; el viento recibe una acción humana sin que haya comparación.
segments: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification,
not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.
teaching.audioText: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification, not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.

prompt.es: Clasifica la imagen principal del diario de Carlos.

choices.text: A simile: the exam is compared to a mountain with like.
A metaphor: the exam is said to be a mountain.
Personification: the mountain acts like a person.

feedback.es: El diario afirma que el examen es una montaña, sin like ni as: es una metáfora; la montaña no hace nada humano.

hint.es: Busca si aparece like o as, y si una cosa simplemente «es» otra.

origin.text: From Carlos's diary: 'This week the final exam is a mountain, and I am still at the start, looking up at a top that I cannot see through the clouds.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom se volvió tan ocupado como una abeja.»

feedback.es: As busy as a bee es el símil fijo de as + adjetivo + as; el adjetivo describe la cualidad típica de la abeja.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que describe a quien no para de trabajar.

origin.text: As soon as the exams began, Tom became as ___ as a bee: he studied at lunch, on the bus and even while he waited for his coffee.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Toda la ciudad duerme en silencio cuando cae la noche.»

answer.text: The whole city sleeps quietly when night falls

feedback.es: Es personificación: la ciudad hace algo humano, dormir; when night falls indica el momento.

hint.es: Sujeto + verbo humano + quietly + when night falls.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué figura prefiere la autora.

choices.text: The one that compares the noise with a machine.
The one that turns the sky into an artist.
The one that treats the storm as a character.

feedback.es: Prefiere la personificación porque convierte la tormenta en una persona; el símil del tren y la metáfora del pintor los presenta sin preferirlos.

origin.audio: In today's episode the writer compares three ways of describing a storm. First she says the storm was as loud as a train, which is a simile. Then she says the sky was an angry painter throwing grey paint everywhere, which is a metaphor. Finally she writes that the wind shouted at the village, and she explains that this is personification. She prefers the third, because it makes the storm feel like a person.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la figura que usa.

pairs: My brother is as quiet as a mouse in class.
The committee is a mountain of reports.
The old clock refused to work on Monday.
The committee meets every Tuesday morning.

feedback.es: El conector as…as marca el símil, «X is a Y» la metáfora, y un objeto que se niega a trabajar es personificación.

pairs: My brother is as quiet as a mouse in class.
The committee is a mountain of reports.
The old clock refused to work on Monday.
The committee meets every Tuesday morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «La tormenta golpeó el pueblo como un tren.»

feedback.es: Like + nombre forma el símil: delante de a train no se puede usar as, que se reserva para as…as o para funciones.

origin.text: The storm hit the town ___ a train, and for an hour nobody in the village dared to leave home.

prompt.es: Escucha a la profesora y elige qué frase del borrador es una metáfora.

choices.text: The one that says the exam simply is a mountain.
The one that compares the exam with climbing a mountain.
The one that says the mountain watches the students.

feedback.es: La frase que afirma que el examen es una montaña, sin conector, es la metáfora; comparar con escalar es un símil y la montaña que vigila es personificación.

origin.audio: Our teacher read three sentences from student drafts. The first said that the exam was as difficult as climbing a mountain. The second said that the exam was a mountain. The third said that the mountain was watching the students and waiting for them to make a mistake. She explained that only one of them is a metaphor, and she warned us that the third, although more original, risks sounding exaggerated if the topic is only a school test.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué implica la profesora sobre la tercera frase.

choices.text: It is wrong, because a mountain cannot act like a person.
It is original, but it may sound exaggerated for the topic.
It is the best, because exaggerated images always work well.

feedback.es: Reconoce su originalidad («more original»), pero avisa de que puede sonar exagerada para un simple examen.

origin.audio: Our teacher read three sentences from student drafts. The first said that the exam was as difficult as climbing a mountain. The second said that the exam was a mountain. The third said that the mountain was watching the students and waiting for them to make a mistake. She explained that only one of them is a metaphor, and she warned us that the third, although more original, risks sounding exaggerated if the topic is only a school test.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los poetas suelen atribuir sentimientos humanos a las cosas.»

feedback.es: Attribute X to Y es la colocación precisa para adjudicar una cualidad o emoción a algo; es la base de la personificación.

origin.text: Poets often ___ human feelings to things: when the sea is angry or the wind whispers, the writer is giving nature a human character of its own.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende el autor sobre los símiles con as…as?

choices.text: Similes can be fresh, but the as…as pattern makes them predictable.
Teachers are mostly right: as…as similes rarely surprise anybody.
Similes are fine; predictable comparisons are the real problem.

feedback.es: El autor separa la estructura, que es válida, de la falta de ideas frescas: no culpa a los símiles, sino a las comparaciones previsibles.

origin.text: Some teachers say that every as…as simile is a cliché. I am not so sure. 'As busy as a bee' is tired, certainly, but 'as quiet as a library at midnight' still surprises the reader. The problem is not the structure; it is the lack of fresh ideas behind it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le pide la editora a Sam en su correo?

choices.text: To keep the jungle metaphor and renew the tired simile.
To keep both images and move the bee simile elsewhere.
To replace both images with literal descriptions of the office.

feedback.es: La editora elogia la metáfora de la selva y critica el símil de la abeja: pide conservar la primera y cambiar el segundo.

origin.text: Dear Sam, thank you for the draft. Your comparison of the office with a jungle was vivid, but 'as busy as a bee' in the next paragraph is a cliché and hurts it. Please keep the metaphor and replace the simile with a fresher image before Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «La profesora nos pidió establecer una diferencia entre símil y metáfora.»

feedback.es: Draw a distinction between A and B es la colocación formal para distinguir dos cosas (también se acepta draw a line); no se dice «make a difference» con este sentido.

origin.text: The teacher asked us to draw a ___ between a simile and a metaphor, that is, to say exactly how they differ, and most of the class found the exercise harder than we had expected.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige qué deja entender la hablante sobre su hermana.

choices.text: That her sister was offended by the comparison with a fridge.
That her sister's image was funnier than her own.
That her own comparison was more original than her sister's.

feedback.es: Al admitir que la broma de su hermana era mejor que su comparación, deja entender que la imagen de la hermana era más ingeniosa.

origin.audio: I told my sister that her new flat was as cold as a fridge. She laughed and said that the old walls had complained all night. Then I realised that she had answered my simile with personification, and that her joke was better than my comparison.
